differential: Nephrotic syndrome
This is the classic presentation for minimal change disease, the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in this age group.
Allergic reaction
Periorbital angioedema is a common manifestation of an allergic response to food, medication, or environmental triggers in children.
Acute glomerulonephritis
This renal condition causes sodium and water retention leading to edema, which often manifests first in the periorbital region.
Periorbital cellulitis
This is a common infection of the eyelid and surrounding tissues that presents with swelling, though it is often unilateral and inflammatory.
Sinusitis
Inflammation of the adjacent ethmoid sinuses can cause inflammatory edema that drains into the periorbital tissues.
eliminated: Orbital cellulitis
The absence of reported pain with eye movements, proptosis, or vision changes makes this more severe infection unlikely.
Congestive heart failure
Isolated periorbital edema is an atypical primary presentation for heart failure in a child, which usually involves more prominent respiratory or systemic signs.

differential: Nephrotic Syndrome

Allergic Reaction

Acute Glomerulonephritis

Periorbital Cellulitis
This is an infection of the eyelid and surrounding tissues that presents with swelling, though it is often also associated with erythema and warmth.
Sinusitis
Inflammation of the ethmoid sinuses can lead to periorbital edema due to their close anatomical proximity to the orbits.
Minimal Change Disease
